items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: with Elvin Jones. With Buddy of course I was known as a soloist but with a big band you’re only going to get a small chunk of space to solo... And so with Elvin’s band, when they heard me play... The thing is, both of my gigs, when I went with Elvin it was the same thing.

ctx.x: Yeah I want to talk about that a bit later. I was reading in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz there’s an entry on you and your brothers. And I was going to read — you know it’s a challenge, they try to describe musicians’ styles, sometimes in one sentence for space reasons. And I was going to read what they said about you but I’m thinking how would you like an opportunity to describe your own playing and in about twenty words. Can you do that?

Well my playing comes from — the earliest references that I referenced were basically Gerry Mulligan, Prez, Stan Getz, Sonny Rollins, Coltrane. I mean I listened to all those guys. Lester Young was a huge influence on me and even to this day, I went through all the periods of music listening to everybody, studied with everybody that I could. And you know, playing with Elvin you had to play a certain way, or I felt that I did, or more modern, but even now today I go back to Lester Young and the things that I…

Nice. Well I’ll read what they said. They should have called you. In regards to your style, “His style is derived principally from that of John Coltrane to which he adds his own rhythmic looseness and lyricism.

items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: we’re doing a tune that he did with Elvin Jones. I’m doing it on my next recording.

ctx.x: As your careers were expanding did you ever get on the phone with them for advice about a decision you needed to make?

Yeah, especially with Pat, ‘cause Pat was the one who led us all. Pat was out there first. He was the trailblazer. You know I’m the middle, well-adjusted son. But he was the one who took all the blows. He’s the one who got me on Buddy Rich’s band you know. He, you know he would, I’d call him for some advice. Yup. And he’s so knowledgeable. still call him about certain changes. I’ll say, on this tune, actually I just did that recently ‘cause we’re doing a tune that he did with Elvin Jones. I’m doing it on my next recording. And I would call him and say what the hell is this, what is all this stuff. And of course he’s got it all in his head. He’s got all these tunes. And he would give me some ideas. Because not everything is consistent in, even in modal writing, nothing is that consistent and there’s always something new to bridge, something new to…
